changed: Rachel (“Rae”) Fifer’s dances, which always use larks and robins, now also leave out a move name or wording from your own dialect that uses a gendered role word such as “ladies” or “gents”: on her dances that move reads in the app’s own wording (a “ladies chain” reads as the app’s chain). Your dialect itself is not changed, and every other dance still uses it as you wrote it.

`dialectForDance` also drops, for a dance that `requiresLarksRobins`, each of the reader's move substitutions, move wordings and wording branches that holds a gendered role word (gent, gents, gentleman, gentlemen, lady, ladies, woman, women; not “man” or “men”, which are everyday words in German, Danish and Dutch). It returns a copy even when the reader's role terms already say lark and robin, whenever it drops one; the dialect passed in is never changed.
